module_intro: Does not introduce a single new analytical tool. Every concept named -- HTF analysis, daily bias, marking liquidity, session selection, LTF execution, model selection, scalping, execution, management, and review -- was already fully defined in Modules 1-12. This module adds sequencing: a repeatable, time-ordered daily routine organized around three phases that repeat every trading day: Pre-Market (analysis and planning), Session (live monitoring and execution), and Post-Trade (review and journaling).
prerequisites_stated_in_text: Assumes full fluency with Modules 1-12; this module is consolidation, not new instruction.
module_objectives: describe the three phases of the daily trading routine (Pre-Market, Session, Post-Trade) and what belongs in each
run a complete pre-market routine, from HTF analysis through to a written daily bias statement and marked liquidity levels
apply the correct entry model (Buy or Sell) during a live session based on the day's established bias
explain why an incomplete setup (missing a genuine sweep, displacement, or structure shift) should be skipped rather than forced
construct a complete trade journal entry, including context, exact levels, result, and an honestly assessed lesson
explain why a disciplined no-trade day should be recorded as a process success rather than a failure

concepts.name: HTF Analysis (Pre-Market phase)
concepts.definition: The trading day begins, before any lower-timeframe chart is opened, with a review of the daily and 4-hour (or weekly, for a longer-term view) charts: current market structure, the position of price within the relevant dealing range (premium or discount), and any unmitigated higher-timeframe liquidity or PD arrays.
concepts.ict_specific_meaning: A direct application of Module 10's HTF Bias process. Should take a fixed, disciplined block of time -- commonly cited across sources as somewhere between fifteen and ninety minutes depending on a trader's overall routine -- rather than being rushed or skipped.
detection_criteria: Review HTF structure (daily/4-hour) and note current premium/discount position within the relevant dealing range.
concepts.numeric_or_narrative_example: unspecified as a standalone numeric example in this module.
concepts.what_it_tells_the_trader: unspecified beyond establishing the analytical starting point of the day.
beginner_mistakes_or_misinterpretations: Skipping the pre-market phase and attempting to establish bias reactively, in the middle of a live session.
concepts.timeframe_relationship: Daily/4-hour (or weekly) HTF review precedes any LTF chart.
cited_sources_in_text: b2prime.com -- 'ICT Trading Checklist: Pre-Trade Preparation for Serious Traders.'

concepts.name: Daily Bias (Pre-Market phase, applied)
concepts.definition: From the HTF analysis, a single directional statement is formed for the day using Module 10's Daily Bias process: structure, the day's or prior day's opening price, and the nearest unswept liquidity, combined into one explicit bullish, bearish, or neutral call.
concepts.ict_specific_meaning: Ideally written down explicitly before the London or New York session begins.
detection_criteria: Establish daily bias (bullish, bearish, or neutral) using Module 10's process, writing it down explicitly.
concepts.numeric_or_narrative_example: unspecified as a standalone numeric example in this module.
concepts.what_it_tells_the_trader: The single directional call that governs which entry model (Buy or Sell) will be used during the session.
beginner_mistakes_or_misinterpretations: unspecified beyond general daily-routine mistakes listed at module level.

concepts.name: Marking Liquidity (Pre-Market phase, applied)
concepts.definition: With bias established, the specific liquidity levels most relevant to that bias are marked on the chart: the opposing liquidity pool expected to be swept first, and the liquidity pool that will serve as the eventual profit target.
concepts.ict_specific_meaning: The same marking process demonstrated in full in Modules 11 and 12's worked examples, done here as a standing daily habit rather than a one-off exercise.
detection_criteria: Mark major liquidity: the opposing pool expected to be swept, and the target pool the eventual move should be aimed at.
concepts.numeric_or_narrative_example: unspecified as a standalone numeric example in this module.
concepts.what_it_tells_the_trader: The specific price levels to watch during the session for the sweep event and for the eventual target.

framework_placement.comes_after: Feeds into Session phase (Selecting the Appropriate Session, LTF Execution).

concepts.name: Selecting the Appropriate Session
concepts.definition: Using Module 8's session and Kill Zone vocabulary, a specific window (or windows) is chosen for active monitoring.
concepts.ict_specific_meaning: Commonly the London Open Kill Zone and/or the New York Open Kill Zone, with the Asian session reserved mainly for observation per Module 8's 'How to Use Each Session' guidance. Not every session needs to be actively traded; concentrating attention on one or two high-probability windows, rather than monitoring continuously around the clock, is described as more disciplined and sustainable.
detection_criteria: Set session expectations: which Kill Zone(s) will be actively watched, and which will be used only for observation (per Module 8/9's session mapping).
concepts.numeric_or_narrative_example: unspecified as a standalone numeric example in this module.
concepts.what_it_tells_the_trader: Which window(s) deserve full trading attention versus mere observation.

concepts.name: LTF Execution
concepts.definition: Once price approaches a marked liquidity level during the selected session, attention shifts to a lower timeframe (commonly the 5-minute, 3-minute, or 1-minute chart) to watch for the specific sequence from Modules 11 and 12: a liquidity sweep, followed by displacement, a Market Structure Shift, and a retracement into an FVG/Order Block, ideally confirmed by OTE.
concepts.ict_specific_meaning: Sources are consistent that if any single piece of this sequence is missing, the setup should be skipped rather than forced.
detection_criteria: Shift to LTF (5-min, 3-min, or 1-min) once price approaches a marked liquidity level.
Watch for liquidity sweep, displacement, MSS, retracement into FVG/OB, ideally OTE confirmation.
preconditions: Requires Marking Liquidity and Selecting the Appropriate Session.
concepts.numeric_or_narrative_example: unspecified as a standalone numeric example in this module.
concepts.what_it_tells_the_trader: Whether the full entry sequence is confirming at the marked level in real time.

framework_placement.comes_after: Feeds into ICT Buy/Sell Model Selection.

concepts.name: ICT Buy/Sell Model Selection
concepts.definition: Based on the daily bias established earlier, the trader commits to looking only for the matching model -- the ICT Buy Model (Module 11) if bias is bullish, or the ICT Sell Model (Module 12) if bias is bearish -- and deliberately disregards setups pointing the opposite direction.
concepts.ict_specific_meaning: Consistent with the discipline Module 10 describes bias as being specifically designed to enforce.
detection_criteria: If daily bias is bullish, look only for ICT Buy Model setups.
If daily bias is bearish, look only for ICT Sell Model setups.
concepts.numeric_or_narrative_example: unspecified as a standalone numeric example in this module.
concepts.what_it_tells_the_trader: Which of the two complete strategies (Module 11 or 12) is eligible to be traded today.

concepts.name: Trade Execution
concepts.definition: The specific mechanics of placing the trade: setting a limit order at the finalized entry zone (Module 7) or entering at market once a lower-timeframe confirmation fires, setting the stop-loss at the level defined by the sweep (Modules 11-12), setting the take-profit at the identified target liquidity, and calculating position size from the resulting risk distance and a predetermined maximum risk percentage per trade.
concepts.ict_specific_meaning: Maximum risk percentage per trade commonly cited across sources as around 1%, rising to a maximum of about 2% only for higher-conviction setups.
detection_criteria: Set limit order at finalized entry zone, or market entry on LTF confirmation.
Set stop-loss at the sweep-defined level.
Set take-profit at identified target liquidity.
Calculate position size from risk distance and predetermined max risk % per trade.
concepts.numeric_or_narrative_example: unspecified as a standalone numeric example in this module (see Modules 11-12 worked examples).
concepts.what_it_tells_the_trader: The precise mechanical steps for placing a trade once a model is selected and confirmed.
concepts.confidence_note: The specific 1%/2% risk percentage figures are cited as commonly used across sources, not attributed to a single verified ICT primary source.

concepts.name: Trade Management
concepts.definition: Once in a trade, management includes monitoring for signs the original premise is failing (e.g., price beginning to threaten the stop-loss level, or failing to displace as expected after reaching the entry zone), and predetermined rules for adjusting the stop to breakeven or scaling out partial profit at intermediate liquidity levels before the final target is reached.
concepts.ict_specific_meaning: Sources emphasize that these rules should be decided in advance, before the trade is placed, rather than improvised emotionally while the trade is open.
detection_criteria: Monitor for signs the original premise is failing.
Apply predetermined stop-to-breakeven rules.
Apply predetermined partial-profit-scaling rules at intermediate liquidity levels.
concepts.numeric_or_narrative_example: unspecified as a standalone numeric example in this module.
concepts.what_it_tells_the_trader: How to manage risk and lock in profit dynamically once a trade is live.
beginner_mistakes_or_misinterpretations: Improvising management rules emotionally while the trade is open instead of deciding them in advance.

concepts.name: Daily Review/Journaling
concepts.definition: After the session (or trading day) concludes, each trade is logged with its full context: the HTF bias and structure that motivated it, the specific liquidity swept, the session and Kill Zone it occurred in, the exact setup type, the entry/stop/target, the actual result, and an honest note on any mistake made or lesson learned, including whether the trader adhered to their own plan regardless of outcome.
concepts.ict_specific_meaning: Sources are consistent that this adherence-focused, process-oriented review (not just tracking profit and loss) is what allows a trader to identify which specific setups and conditions actually produce good results over time.
detection_criteria: HTF context that was in place when the trade was taken
The bias (bullish/bearish/neutral) and how it was determined
The specific liquidity swept, and the target liquidity aimed at
The session/Kill Zone the setup occurred in
The specific setup/model used (Buy Model, Sell Model, or scalping variant)
The exact entry, stop-loss, and target prices
The invalidation condition that was defined before entry
The actual result (win, loss, breakeven, or scratch)
Any mistake made, including deviations from the plan even on winning trades
The specific lesson drawn, to be checked against future trades of the same type
preconditions: Requires a completed session, whether or not a trade was actually taken.
concepts.numeric_or_narrative_example: unspecified as a standalone numeric example in this module.
concepts.what_it_tells_the_trader: Whether the pre-market plan was actually followed, and which setups/conditions produce good results over time.
common_pairings: HTF Analysis (feeds back into next day's Pre-Market)

framework_placement.comes_before: Requires the Session phase to have concluded.
framework_placement.comes_after: Feeds directly back into the next day's Pre-Market phase, closing the loop.

beginner_mistakes_or_misinterpretations: Journaling only wins and losses (profit and loss) rather than the full context, process adherence, and lessons recommended.
concepts.qualification_or_limits: A day where the plan correctly identified no qualifying setup, and no trade was forced, is recorded as a process success, not as a wasted day.
cited_sources_in_text: journalplus.co -- 'How to Build a Daily Trading Routine That Actually Works' (R-multiple tracking, no-trade-day-as-success framing).

rules.statement: Predetermined maximum risk percentage per trade, commonly cited across sources as around 1%, rising to a maximum of about 2% only for higher-conviction setups.
rules.exceptions_or_qualifiers: Figures are commonly cited across secondary sources, not attributed to a single verified ICT primary source.

rules.statement: Daily Scalping checklist (short, strictly enforced): a clear liquidity draw, a complete Sweep -> Displace -> Retrace -> Enter sequence, a single-impulse objective, and a tight, clearly defined invalidation point. If any single piece is missing, the setup is skipped entirely.
rules.exceptions_or_qualifiers: Scalping is described as fragile -- highly sensitive to spread, slippage, and news risk.

rules.statement: HTF Analysis should take a fixed, disciplined block of time -- commonly cited across sources as somewhere between fifteen and ninety minutes depending on a trader's overall routine.

strategies.name: Daily Scalping

context.htf_bias_required: Daily bias established (per Daily Bias process).
context.other_context: For traders operating on a shorter time horizon within the day.

setup: Apply the same Buy/Sell Model logic (Modules 11-12) with a smaller, single-impulse objective rather than a multi-day swing target.
Confirm a clear liquidity draw is identifiable nearby.
strategies.entry_condition: Enter on a complete sweep-displacement-retracement-entry sequence (the same core sequence as the Buy/Sell Models), targeting only the next nearby liquidity pool rather than a distant higher-timeframe level.
strategies.invalidation_or_stop: A tight, clearly defined invalidation point (mirrors Buy/Sell Model stop logic -- beyond the swept level). If any single required piece (clear liquidity draw, complete sweep-displace-retrace-enter sequence, single-impulse objective, tight invalidation point) is missing, the setup is skipped entirely.
strategies.target_or_exit: The next nearby liquidity pool (single-impulse objective), not a distant HTF level.
trade_management_rules: Described as fragile -- highly sensitive to spread, slippage, and news risk.
missing_elements: Exact numeric definition of 'nearby' liquidity pool or 'single-impulse' distance not given.

relationships.statement: This module's ten concepts are ten checkpoints along one continuous daily loop that repeats indefinitely: pre-market planning leads into session execution, which leads into post-trade review, which directly informs the next day's pre-market planning. Every earlier module feeds into exactly one or more of these ten checkpoints: Modules 1-3 and 10 feed HTF Analysis and Daily Bias; Module 4 feeds Marking Liquidity; Modules 8 and 9 feed Selecting the Appropriate Session; Modules 3-7 feed LTF Execution; Modules 11-12 feed ICT Buy/Sell Model Selection and Daily Scalping; and the discipline threaded throughout the book (patience, waiting for confirmation, respecting invalidation) feeds Trade Execution, Trade Management, and Daily Review/Journaling.

no_trade_conditions.statement: If any single piece of the sweep-displacement-structure-shift sequence is missing (no genuine sweep, no real displacement, no confirmed structure shift), the setup should be skipped entirely rather than forced. A trader who takes a trade missing one of these pieces is using a different, unvalidated approach that happens to share some of its vocabulary.

If the selected Kill Zone window closes without a qualifying setup, no trade is the correct and disciplined outcome. A day where the plan correctly identified no qualifying setup, and no trade was forced, is recorded as a process success, not a wasted day.

module_review_notes.beginner_summary: A trading day follows one repeatable three-phase loop. In Pre-Market, the trader reviews HTF structure, establishes a written daily bias, marks relevant liquidity levels, and decides which session(s) to actively watch. In Session, the trader observes price during the chosen Kill Zone, waits for the complete sweep-displacement-structure-shift sequence, and applies the matching Buy or Sell Model to enter, manage, and exit the trade -- or takes no trade at all if the sequence never completes. In Post-Trade, every trade (and every no-trade day) is logged in detail: context, exact levels, actual result, and an honest lesson -- feeding directly back into the next day's Pre-Market phase.
module_review_notes.concept_relationships_summary: HTF Analysis, Daily Bias, and Marking Liquidity belong to the Pre-Market phase. Selecting the Appropriate Session, LTF Execution, ICT Buy/Sell Model Selection, Daily Scalping, Trade Execution, and Trade Management belong to the Session phase. Daily Review/Journaling belongs to the Post-Trade phase and feeds directly back into the next day's Pre-Market phase, making the whole routine cyclical rather than linear.
module_review_notes.practical_chart_exercise: Write out a complete, hypothetical pre-market plan for a single trading day: state the HTF structure you are assuming, write an explicit daily bias statement, name the specific liquidity levels you would mark, and state which session(s) you would actively watch versus only observe. Then write a matching post-trade journal entry assuming the setup played out exactly as planned, and a second journal entry assuming it did not complete (no genuine sweep occurred) and no trade was taken.
self_test_questions: What are the three phases of the daily trading routine described in this module, and what is the primary purpose of each?
Why should HTF Analysis and Daily Bias be completed before the trading session begins, rather than during it?
What should a trader do if, during the Session phase, price approaches a marked liquidity level but never produces a genuine sweep and structure shift?
Why does this module recommend recording a disciplined no-trade day in the trading journal with the same care as an actual trade?
Name at least five specific pieces of information this module recommends recording for every trade.
common_misconceptions: Believing this daily routine is a new, separate strategy rather than a sequencing of everything covered in Modules 1 through 12.
Skipping the pre-market phase and attempting to establish bias and mark liquidity reactively, in the middle of a live session.
Forcing a trade when part of the sweep-displacement-structure-shift sequence is missing, rather than accepting a no-trade outcome.
Journaling only wins and losses (profit and loss) rather than the full context, process adherence, and lessons this module recommends recording.
